sections.heading: S2. Evidence contracts and boundary conventions
paragraphs: Fix one evidence-bearing task and its finite sentence-ID domain. Its reference family consists of one or more nonempty sets. Several alternatives may support the same task; an output need contain one complete alternative, not the union of all alternatives. In the authored finite certificate, alternatives may overlap. That broader certificate class is explicitly different from claiming that every such family occurs in the native dataset. No independent domain expert adjudicated reference completeness or correctness.

A and B are ordered lists without duplicate IDs. Empty input lists are admitted in boundary checks, but an empty input cannot be annotation-sufficient when all references are nonempty. A valid generated order likewise contains distinct IDs. For nonnegative integer k, its prefix contains the first min(k,length) entries. Cap zero yields the empty output. Capacities beyond the union size do not pad or invent IDs. An ID outside the output order has infinite rank; the infinity convention concerns absence, not a numeric rank inserted into the response.

Full containment S asks whether at least one reference is a subset of the entire output. First-three asks the same question after an additional prefix-three operation. Exact-annotated E asks whether the entire output set equals one listed alternative. An empty output scores zero for all three on evidence-bearing tasks. The original broader task audit also has insufficient-evidence tasks with a separate label/empty-evidence contract; those are not relabeled as members of the current 309-task pair bank.

These endpoints can disagree legitimately. Adding an unannotated ID preserves full containment but can destroy exact matching. Moving a required ID behind position three preserves the full set but can destroy first-three acceptance. An unannotated ID is not automatically semantically irrelevant, and an exact-match failure is not automatically an incorrect answer. Conversely, if the application truly requires a short ranked rationale, its first-three failure is operationally real even when the evidence still occurs later. Correct labels are supplied by the auditor throughout; label prediction, retrieval from a corpus, native aggregate F1, and model faithfulness are outside the executed contract.

E(X) = bb(1)[exists R in cal(R): X = R]

sections.heading: S3. Stable operators and information permissions
paragraphs: The complete round-robin order V is constructed before the output cap. Visit A's first entry, B's first entry, A's second entry, B's second entry, continuing through the longer list. Append an ID only on its first visit. Thus V contains each element of the union once. Define C as the intersection. P is the C-subsequence of V followed by the non-C subsequence of V. This is a stable partition, not sorting by ID value, reference membership, or an inferred semantic relevance score.

The policy input is exactly A, B, and k. Reference families are passed only to the scoring/auditing stage. The construction code does not receive reference labels, completed-reference ranks, the both-input-sufficient inclusion flag, or a held-out score. Completion-rank and removed-ID certificates are gold-aware explanations after construction; they are not exposed as routing features. A policy that used those certificates to select its output would have different information rights and could not inherit the label-blind comparison.

The earlier agreement-first rule obtained the relative order of common IDs from a left-priority construction. The current stable partition obtains both class orders from V. At capacity three, every common ID fits because each input has at most three IDs; set-based endpoint results match the saved priority audit. At capacities one and two, a prefix may contain only some common IDs, so the change in internal class order matters. These small-cap results are not described as an identical rerun of the previous constructor.

An interleaving, a common-item promotion, truncating an input before union construction, and truncating the completed union are different interventions. Only the last specified sequence is analyzed. An implementation that drops entries from A or B before deduplication, sorts common IDs numerically, consults a reference, or silently fills an empty intersection with oracle IDs changes the experiment. The reproducibility check must compare exact ordered outputs as well as their scores: tied scores alone cannot establish that the intended constructor was executed.

algorithm.caption: Deterministic label-blind constructor. References are not an argument. The scorer is a separate audit step.
lines: INPUT A, B, nonnegative integer k; initialize V=[], seen=empty set.
For index i from 0 to max(len(A),len(B))-1, visit A[i] then B[i] when present.
Append a visited ID to V only if it is not already in seen; then add it to seen.
Set C=set(A) intersect set(B).
Set P=[x in V with x in C] followed by [x in V with x not in C].
Return the prefix of V and the prefix of P of length min(k,len(V)).
Only after outputs are frozen, evaluate the original nonempty reference alternatives.

sections.heading: S4. Completion ranks and the single-window proof
paragraphs: Fix any complete distinct-ID order L and nonempty alternative R. If every member of R appears in L, the smallest prefix containing R ends at its last required ID. Its completion rank is therefore the maximum of the member ranks. If at least one member is absent, no finite prefix completes R and that alternative's completion rank is infinity. The family is accepted as soon as its earliest-completing alternative is accepted, so take the minimum over alternatives. This establishes the formula in both the finite and absent-reference cases without assuming equal reference lengths or disjoint alternatives.

To prove the prefix identity in both directions, suppose k is at least the minimum completion rank. A minimizing finite alternative has every member ranked at most k and is a subset of the prefix, giving sufficiency. Conversely, if the prefix is sufficient, some alternative lies entirely inside it, so its maximum member rank is at most k and the minimum completion rank is no larger. If all alternatives have infinite completion rank, no finite prefix passes. The minimum is attained whenever it is finite because the recorded family is finite.

Let b and p be the baseline and promoted completion thresholds. If p is below b, the promoted output alone passes exactly for p <= k < b. Before p both fail; from b onward both pass. If b is below p, baseline alone passes exactly for b <= k < p. Equal thresholds give ties at every capacity, including the case where both are infinite. When one threshold is infinite the interval is unbounded above over unrestricted capacities; on the audited finite range it is intersected with zero through six. For two permutations of the same full union, reachability is shared, so either both thresholds are finite or both infinite.

This proves a single contiguous non-tie interval and a single polarity for each fixed pair under full containment. It does not prove a one-capacity interval. A manually authored teaching example uses A=(1,2,0), B=(4,5,0), but changes the reference family to the singleton alternative {0}. This is not the saved task's original annotation. V=(1,4,2,5,0) has threshold five; P=(0,1,4,2,5) has threshold one. Gains then span capacities one through four. The saved bank's observed width-one intervals are a property of that bank, not a theorem about stable promotion.

Exact matching lacks the same monotonicity: a prefix can equal an alternative and then stop equaling it after an extra ID is added. First-three is monotone only until its effective cap reaches three and then freezes. The rank formula can describe that frozen endpoint by replacing k with min(k,3), but increasing generated k beyond three cannot restore a reference whose earliest required rank exceeds three. Interpreting the rank threshold as a model confidence or a semantic correctness guarantee would add an unsupported assumption.
equations: S_k(P) - S_k(V) = cases(1 & p <= k < b, -1 & b <= k < p, 0 & "otherwise")

sections.heading: S5. Removed IDs and an exact loss certificate
paragraphs: Write Bk and Pk for the baseline and promoted prefix sets. A common ID x already in Bk has common-class rank at most its original V rank. Moving the entire common subsequence to the front gives it that common-class rank, never a later one. Thus every baseline-selected common ID remains selected. A noncommon ID retained by Pk has noncommon rank at most k minus the number of common IDs filling the promoted prefix; enough earlier noncommon positions therefore existed in the baseline prefix to contain it. Equivalently, stable promotion cannot add a previously unselected noncommon ID. These statements also hold when k exceeds the union size because both outputs then contain the full union.

Consequently, removed IDs D=Bk minus Pk are noncommon, and added IDs H=Pk minus Bk are common. The two output sets have equal size, so D and H have equal size. If a baseline-complete reference contains only common IDs, it survives. More generally, a baseline-complete reference survives exactly when it avoids D, because all of its remaining IDs were already in Bk and are retained. This gives a useful necessary risk condition without asserting that common IDs are true or false.

A full loss occurs if and only if at least one reference was complete in Bk, every such complete reference intersects D, and no reference is complete in Pk. The final condition matters: destroying all previously complete alternatives does not prevent a different alternative from becoming complete using the newly added common IDs. Checking only one preferred annotation would also be inadequate; the loss certificate must quantify over the original family. The saved output stores the relevant removals, additions, and alternatives so a reader can audit this distinction.

There is a separate universal boundary. If two equal-size output sets differ, choose an ID x present in the baseline and absent from the other output. Under the admissible singleton reference family {{x}}, the baseline passes and the other fails. Therefore, without restrictions on possible references, a same-size transformation that changes the set cannot guarantee full-containment no-regression for every family. This is a quantified annotation-contract statement, not an impossibility result for useful skill integration. It does not say every changed output loses on the actual task, and it does not license choosing a favorable artificial reference after seeing model behavior.

The universal singleton construction need not satisfy the both-input-sufficient restriction used in S6: the removed noncommon ID may occur in only one input. Its counterexample therefore cannot refute that conditional theorem. The order of quantifiers matters: a guarantee for every reference family is stronger than a guarantee only for families witnessed in both complete inputs.

D subset.eq (A union B) ∖ C, quad H subset.eq C

sections.heading: S6. Conditional cap-four theorem and its limits
paragraphs: The theorem assumes: A and B each contain at most three distinct IDs; each full input contains at least one complete nonempty reference alternative; the complete deduplicated union is formed before truncation; the common and noncommon classes preserve their relative V order; and the endpoint is full-output containment. The two inputs may contain different reference alternatives. This is an annotation condition on full stored lists, not an empirical Q gate on independently authored programs and not a guarantee that each shortened input is sufficient.

Partition by the common-set size c. If c=0, P=V exactly, so no baseline-success-to-promotion-failure transition is possible at any capacity. This establishes no-loss even if both prefixes fail. If c>=2, the union has at most 3+3-2=4 IDs. At k>=4 both outputs therefore contain the union, and the sufficient-input assumption implies success. If c=1, the union has at most five IDs. At k>=4 the promoted prefix retains the common ID and omits at most one union ID. An omitted noncommon ID belongs to only one input, so the other input is entirely retained; its complete reference alternative remains. These cases exhaust the input class.

The distinction between success and no-loss is indispensable. Take A=(0,1,2), B=(3,4,5), with alternatives {0,1,2} and {3,4,5}. Both full inputs are sufficient, but at capacity four both orders are (0,3,1,4) and neither alternative is complete. The implication 'baseline passes implies promotion passes' is true because the antecedent is false; unconditional promoted success is false. This is the condition that exposed the initial verifier's overstrong assertion. Likewise, the theorem allows gains: S4's authored common-singleton example has a capacity-four gain. The bank's all-tie result above three is not the theorem's conclusion.

The input-length restriction is substantive. In a manually derived illustration, let A=(1,2,3,0), B=(4,5,0), with alternatives {1,2,3} and {4,5}. The complete inputs are sufficient and the partition is stable, but one input has length four. V=(1,4,2,5,3,0) at cap four passes via {4,5}; P=(0,1,4,2,5,3) at cap four completes neither alternative. This is an explanatory counterexample outside the theorem's class, not an additional observed task or a rerun of the finite benchmark.

First-three and exact endpoints remain outside the guarantee. A generated fourth ID can complete a reference that first-three never reads, while exact matching may reject a sufficient superset. Truncating inputs before union formation also changes which alternatives can survive. Empty references are deliberately excluded: admitting an empty valid alternative would make full containment vacuously pass, changing the meaning of qualification and all cap-zero results. Boundary handling is part of the proposition, not a detail to fix after seeing the score.

paragraphs: The preserved actual diagnostic witness is scifact_v4_382. A=(1,2,0) contains alternative {1,2}; B=(4,5,0) contains alternative {4,5}. The shared ID is zero. V=(1,4,2,5,0) and P=(0,1,4,2,5). At cap three the baseline retains IDs one and two, whereas promotion removes two and adds zero. It thereby completes neither original alternative. The inputs, union, output count, references, and noncommon order are fixed; common-class priority identifies this particular transition.

At cap four, promoted (0,1,4,2) again includes {1,2}. Its first-three prefix remains (0,1,4), so generated length and evaluator length tell different stories. At cap five or six, both operators emit all five IDs and full containment passes; first-three still reads the same failing promoted prefix. No claim about the semantic irrelevance of sentence zero is needed for the set calculation. The two recorded losses in the bank are ordered pair views, not two independent trials of real skills.

The separate authored certificate enumerates ID universes zero through six, all distinct-ID ordered inputs of lengths zero through three whose union is that universe, and one/two-alternative families witnessed in both full inputs. It covers 3,046 input pairs and 122,571 families, including overlapping alternatives, at seven capacities. Lexicographic witness selection records the smallest union size and then total input length where losses occur. This is minimality within the declared exhaustive finite class and selection order, not a global minimal natural-language counterexample.

sections.heading: S8. Paired denominators and weighting reversal
paragraphs: A pair-capacity transition is a matched comparison: score the baseline and promotion on the same ordered inputs, task references, endpoint, and cap. A gain is a zero-to-one change; a loss is one-to-zero; ties include both failure/failure and success/success. The pair-pooled contrast equals gains minus losses divided by all retained pairs. Dropping unchanged failures, empty outputs, or zero-common pairs changes the denominator and cannot be called the same effect. A separate qualified-history target would additionally need actual independent authoring and an observed Q gate, which are absent.

The full cohort contains 22,794 ordered pairs nested within 309 tasks and 204 recorded components. Its both-full-input-sufficient stratum contains 12,067 pairs within 308 tasks and 203 components. At low capacities this stratum does not require each input's own truncated prefix to be sufficient. The stratum is selected by auditor references, after the response bank exists; its means cannot be treated as qualification yield or as an unbiased sample of useful skills. Components describe recorded structural grouping, not guaranteed semantic independence.

For pair-pooled weighting, each pair receives equal mass. For equal-task weighting, first average pair changes within each task, then average tasks. For equal-component weighting, additionally average task means within each component, then average components. These summaries differ whenever pair counts or task counts differ. In the sufficient-input stratum, cap-one gains 565 and losses 1,409 give -844/12067=-0.0699428193 approximately. The predeclared equal-component result is +3363459013/266277211200=+0.0126314190 approximately; the equal-task result is approximately +0.01013. The sign change is descriptive sensitivity to unit weighting, not a numerical inconsistency.

A new teaching example makes the mechanism transparent without claiming to reproduce the bank: component X has one task with 100 pairs and pair contrast -0.20; component Y has one task with 10 pairs and contrast +0.30. Pair pooling gives (-20+3)/110=-17/110, approximately -0.15455. Equal-component weighting gives (-0.20+0.30)/2=+0.05. Different probability measures answer different questions even on identical rows. The actual bank's exact fractions above are saved results; these two invented components are only an arithmetic explanation.

Computational size must remain separate from independent sample size. Seven caps create 159,558 pair-capacity contracts, two operators create 319,116 outputs, and three endpoints create 957,348 score cells. None creates an additional task or independent history. A future inferential plan would declare whether histories and source families are fixed or sampled and account for both dependencies. The current exact enumerations support finite descriptive claims without a population confidence interval or power guarantee.

sections.heading: S9. Complete capacity results and endpoint tradeoffs
paragraphs: The following table restores pass counts and ties that the compact main table omits for space. Every row retains the same 22,794 pairs. At cap one the pooled full-containment change is (565-2700)/22794; at cap two it is (95-25)/22794; at cap three it is -2/22794. These pair-pooled fractions are not the equal-component primary summaries. For example, cap-three equal-component difference is -1/13056, demonstrating why the displayed transition count is not itself the component average.

The full-containment boundary and the first-three plateau must be read together. For k>=3, first-three evaluates the same three leading IDs at every generated cap, so its zero-gain/two-loss pattern persists through six. Full containment sees newly appended IDs and has no transitions at caps four through six on this bank, although both methods' absolute pass counts rise. Identical scores between methods do not mean all tasks pass: even cap six leaves 2,255 union-unreachable pairs. A complete union cannot create a missing reference ID.

Exact-annotated changes follow a different pattern: at cap one they coincide with sufficient changes for this bank; at cap two promotion has 66 exact gains and no exact losses; from cap three onward all exact comparisons tie. The contract, not the theorem, determines this pattern. The S4 rank proof is deliberately not cited as an exact-match guarantee. Original annotations may omit semantically valid evidence, so the result is phrased as exact reference agreement rather than truth recovery.

The inherited agreement-only audit further shows why an apparently favorable score can be misleading. Against left-union, intersection-only has 13,855 sufficient losses while also having 2,328 exact gains and 22 exact losses. Under equal-component weighting it emits sufficient/exact scores 0.290889/0.150539, compared with a pairwise output-length-matched uniform control at 0.356638/0.221823. It outputs fewer IDs, and the matched random control makes the resulting score difference interpretable. None of these proportions is a success rate for newly executed skills.

sections.heading: S10. Strong baselines and restricted selection rights
paragraphs: Simple controls are strong because they isolate what the proposed signal contributes. Round-robin preserves interleaving without reading references. Stable promotion changes class priority while matching output count. Intersection-only tests abstaining from noncommon material, but must be compared with an exactly matched-length random subset. Left-priority and reversal controls expose input-order dependence. A negative control may outperform a proposed rule without thereby becoming an independently validated deployment policy. All selection rights and candidate membership remain part of the experiment.

The inherited component-fold selector chooses among exactly four declared rules: left-union, round-robin, agreement-first, and agreement-only. Every sufficient-objective fold selects round-robin; every exact-objective fold selects agreement-only. Thus cross-fitting adds no score through variable selection. Its four-rule per-pair gold oracle reaches 0.840200 sufficient and 0.153696 exact, but the excluded disagreement-first control reaches 0.842416 sufficient. This is not a contradiction: a maximum over one candidate set does not bound a method outside that set. Retrospective admission of the negative control would be a new selection decision.

Component-held-out choice makes local access rights clear but cannot undo prior exposure of the annotations, tasks, and diagnostic design. Cawley and Talbot [21] is cited only within its recorded metadata/abstract scope; we transfer no unread full-text theorem. Self-consistency [20] is a separate final-answer aggregation mechanism with sampled reasoning paths, not a native implementation of our sentence-ID intersection. ERASER [4] supplies a rationale-evaluation distinction, not proof that an annotation-contained output is faithful to a model. SkillsBench [19] is the versioned release artifact, not a paper performance baseline run here.

Future native or inspired comparisons need their own explicit contract. Conservative replay must be allowed to reject, narrow, split, or fall back; an always-merge straw controller would suppress its strength. Typed migration needs caller/resource updates and behavioral acceptance beyond schema legality. Runtime routing/assembly must be charged for its decisions and any LLM calls. A fixed-pool adapter and the full native system answer different questions: identical candidate bytes may be appropriate for the first but remove a native system's candidate-generation mechanism from the second. No imported score is placed beside the local finite counts.

sections.heading: S12. Failed verification and the corrected claim
paragraphs: The initial frozen verifier tested a statement stronger than the registered theorem: for all individually sufficient inputs, the promoted output must pass at cap at least four. S6's disjoint-input example refutes that stronger statement because promotion leaves both failing prefixes unchanged. The intended theorem only excludes a baseline-success-to-promotion-failure transition. A failed check can therefore reveal a verifier specification error rather than a reason to change or hide the underlying analysis. Here the original failure is part of the public evidence trail.

The frozen initial verifier digest is 27b8657b52b0d675d150c16e66bbd765b6dedfd2cfda05662a9a1420bff7f391. That source snapshot remains unchanged. The corrected executed checker is separately frozen and bound by 3f55cfb7520aa4db75765541fe21afee07f691f8d3a15866f2b4319c6d5175e7. Its verifier_lock.json records the narrow correction: check the registered no-loss implication instead of universal success. No plan, source input, analysis output, sufficient-input stratum, or endpoint was changed to make a scientific result pass.

The successful verification_02/verification.json reports eleven input-hash checks, 22,794 pair certificates, 159,558 pair-capacity contracts, 957,348 endpoint cells, 3,387 transition events, 63 aggregate rows, 609 risk-stratum rows, and 857,997 authored reference-capacity cells. Separately written prefix-set logic and bitmask enumeration avoid importing the analyzer's constructor functions. This provides error-detection diversity within one author's work; it is neither an independent laboratory replication nor an external expert endorsement.

The finite certificate includes zero-cap, empty-common, empty-input, beyond-union-cap, and absent-reference cases. Under nonempty references, an empty input never enters the both-sufficient class. Equal or infinite completion ranks tie; source families with no fully reachable alternative never become successes by reordering. The corrected no-loss implication is consistent with unchanged failures in these cases. Historical analysis and verification commands are retained in VERIFICATION_HISTORY.json; the compact rewrite does not rewrite a failed attempt as a successful original execution.

sections.heading: S13. Prospective independent-history protocol
paragraphs: This section is an unexecuted feasibility design inherited from the research program, not additional evidence. An event fixes a common ancestor, source family, resources, tool rights, and independently authored branch changes A/B. Authors may inspect development D but neither each other's patch nor auditor-only Q/S labels. Freeze proposal caps, duplicate detection, and proposal order before qualification. Qualification is an observed isolated-branch gain against the same ancestor on Q, not a role assigned by a critic and not the annotation condition of the current stored input stratum.

The bounded feasibility plan proposes three independently sourced families and four attempted A/B histories per family: twelve attempts, not twelve guaranteed eligible pairs or a powered confirmatory sample. Each branch has at most two proposals. On twenty source-disjoint Q tasks and one predeclared seed, require each branch to exceed the ancestor by at least two successful tasks. Freeze all proposals before Q, return no Q feedback to authors, and select the first passing proposal in fixed order. At most five configurations, ancestor plus four proposals, imply at most 100 task-arm evaluations per history; these are not necessarily 100 API requests, and generation/tool costs remain additional.

An eligible pair would receive fresh reset S0/A/B/AB evaluations on twenty previously unexposed S tasks with two predeclared seeds: at most 4×20×2=160 final task-arm-seed evaluations per eligible pair. The target compares joint availability against an equal mixture of isolated branches, not a best branch picked after viewing S. Source-family/history weighting must be fixed before S. If no history qualifies, retain yield zero and the behavioral effect null; weakening the Q gate after observing AB would define a different target.

An interaction contrast is not the same target. In a teaching cell (S0,A,B,AB)=(0,1,1,1), the interaction AB-A-B+S0 is -1 but the joint-minus-mean-isolated contrast is zero. In (1,1,1,0), that primary contrast is -1. These arithmetic cells are not assigned observations. Trace availability, actual routing, actual reading, and assembled bytes separately, because installing a skill is not the same intervention as forced activation or exposing its contents to the final model.

Before any real model call, separately specify the actual model identity, allowed transmitted data, request/token/cost limits, tokenizer, reset policy, timeouts, and deployment endpoint. Rejected proposals, repairs, loading/cache, routing, assembly, retries, and final runs must be charged. Conservative baselines may fall back or defer, but completion, deployment coverage, deferral and total cost must be reported together. A policy that refuses every difficult task is not unconditionally successful. Candidate-conditioned stress cases, mixed feedback rights, or a revised candidate class require their own labels and comparisons.

sections.heading: S14. Admission decisions and falsification ledger
paragraphs: The current audit supports an engineering admission decision, not deployment of the highest finite score. Before treating a negative result as semantic interference, check that the response can express a valid answer, that all original alternatives are preserved, that the grader applies the declared ranking/cap, and that the comparison changes only its intended mechanism. If a same-set reordering changes a score, that is evidence about the ranked contract; it does not by itself establish loss of full evidence. If a merge actually omits a required ID under a cap, omission is a narrower observed mechanism than general semantic conflict.

Falsification must be attached to a claim. The explanation that joint use lost annotated evidence is weakened when complete output sets retain it and only first-three fails. The explanation that common-item priority is beneficial in general is refuted by the saved sufficient-input witness; the stronger universal no-loss claim for unrestricted changed sets is refuted by S5's singleton construction. The conditional cap-four theorem survives those examples because it states narrower assumptions. A prospective natural-skill effect would require fresh histories and could be weakened if its negative contrast disappears under matched ordering, actual tokenizer length, information rights, unchanged resources, and the frozen endpoint.

The future decision ledger must retain assigned availability cells, invalid outputs, agent-caused timeouts, nonactivation, deliberate deferral, and unresolved external outages. External outages need an explicit missingness policy and bounded summaries rather than silent deletion or automatic success. Repeated seeds share histories; repeated tasks may share source families. Qualification yield, paired variability, and feasible cost from an independently sourced pilot should inform later precision planning, without turning the current zero-history ledger into a power calculation.

The final compact conclusion is intentionally narrower than a broad skill-composition claim: under a specified finite annotation contract, stable promotion can displace completion, a rank threshold determines its capacity window, and declared weighting can reverse an aggregate sign. The complete historical manuscript remains in inherited.paper to preserve prior diagnoses, sensitivity envelopes, comparison discussions, and source scopes. Historical version progression is an audit trail in the supplement, not a stack of separate claims of new behavioral evidence.

sections.heading: S15. The conditional reference class and label-blind switch
paragraphs: This section distinguishes four objects often collapsed into one word, useful: a reference alternative contained by a fixed output; containment by the complete input before truncation; independently measured skill improvement on Q; and deployment correctness. Only the first two enter the new mathematics. A and B are ordered, distinct-ID input lists. Their complete union order V alternates A then B by position and removes repeated occurrences. P is a stable partition of V into common IDs followed by noncommon IDs. No reference, task label, prior score, or judge feedback enters either order.

Fix A, B and a nonnegative integer cap k before choosing a reference family. X and Y are the ID sets of the equal-size capped outputs V_k and P_k. Consider every finite nonempty family of nonempty reference alternatives having at least one alternative contained in full A and at least one contained in full B. The two witnessing alternatives may coincide or overlap; they need not exhaust the family or the input. Extra alternatives may use IDs outside the union. The forward guarantee covers all such families. We do not assume the annotations enumerate every semantically correct answer.

The guard accepts if X=Y, or all of A is retained in Y, or all of B is retained in Y. It compares IDs and sets only. The guarded output is exactly P_k on acceptance and exactly V_k on rejection. This is a cap-dependent switch between two complete candidate outputs, not an LLM router, skill assembler, label-aware oracle or a task-specific learned selector. An observed both-sufficient flag is computed later to describe which rows satisfy the theorem; it is not an input to the guard.

Two quantifier orders must not be exchanged. The theorem fixes A/B/k and asks whether promotion is safe for every admissible reference family. It does not inspect the actual family and find the largest set of acceptable promotions. The latter task could use an actual reference-aware certificate for a retrospective audit, but exposing that certificate to a deployed constructor changes its information rights. No such oracle policy is scored as a reference-blind method here.
equations: G(A,B,k) = bb(1)[X = Y or "set"(A) subset.eq Y or "set"(B) subset.eq Y]

Accept if their ID sets coincide, or P_k contains every ID of A, or P_k contains every ID of B.
Return P_k on acceptance; otherwise return V_k and record a fallback.
Only after construction, read the original reference family to score endpoints and record descriptive strata.

sections.heading: S16. Exact conditional theorem and reverse counterfamily
paragraphs: Theorem. For fixed A/B/k and equal-cardinality X,Y contained in the same union, the guard is true if and only if full-containment success of X implies success of Y for every reference family in the conditional class of S15. The algebraic theorem is not restricted to stable promotion; the concrete operators provide the particular X,Y tested. Nonempty alternatives exclude automatic success from an empty rationale. This statement promises no-loss, not successful output on every task.

Forward, case one: X=Y. Every alternative is either contained in both sets or neither, so scores coincide. Forward, case two: A is wholly retained in Y. By membership in the conditional class, some alternative R_A is contained in A. Transitivity puts R_A inside Y, so Y passes regardless of whether X passes. Case three for B is identical. This proof allows unequal input lengths, overlapping alternatives, more than two alternatives, incomplete reference inventories, and extra alternatives outside the union. None of those variations changes the implication.

Reverse: suppose all guard clauses are false. Because X and Y have the same finite cardinality and differ, there is an x in X outside Y. Since neither full input is inside Y, choose a_out from A outside Y and b_out from B outside Y. If x belongs to A, use {x} as the A-witnessing alternative; otherwise use {a_out}. If x belongs to B, use {x} as the B-witnessing alternative; otherwise use {b_out}. Remove duplicate singleton alternatives if they coincide. At most two nonempty alternatives remain. Each complete input contains one, at least one equals {x}, and none is inside Y. Therefore X succeeds and Y fails on this admissible family. This explicitly refutes universal conditional safety whenever the guard rejects.

The reverse construction proves restricted maximality. A binary switch that sometimes emits P_k and otherwise emits V_k cannot safely accept any rejected shape while preserving this universal conditional promise: that shape has the constructed counterfamily. Maximality is relative to both the two-candidate policy class and the quantified reference class. It is not Pareto-optimality under the actual annotations, semantic correctness, expected utility, token cost, or arbitrary new output construction. Actual reference knowledge could safely accept more shapes, and the saved bank contains two gains that this conservative guard declines.

Equal cardinality is used only to turn X!=Y into an ID removed from X. With unequal sizes, replace the equality clause by X subset Y. If no ID is removed, monotonicity of full containment gives the forward case; if an ID is removed and neither complete input is retained, the same singleton construction works. We do not implement or score an unequal-budget policy. The equality-based guard must not be copied to a different-length output comparison without revisiting that premise.

At k=0, X=Y is empty and the guard accepts. With nonempty alternatives both scores fail, hence no-loss holds without success. If an input is empty, no nonempty reference family can make it sufficient; the conditional class is vacuous. For the present stable constructor, an empty input also leaves P=V and satisfies the guard, so no empty eligible population is manufactured. An empty common set leaves P=V at every cap. These endpoints are covered explicitly by the separate verifier.

sections.heading: S17. Sharp general-length boundary and authored counterexamples
paragraphs: Corollary. If both input lengths are at most d>=2 and the stable partition is formed from the complete alternating union before capping, every cap k>=2d-2 satisfies the structural guard. Conditional no-loss follows from S16. This generalizes length three/cap four without silently removing its assumptions. It is a uniform worst-case bound: particular shapes can be accepted at a much smaller cap, which is the reason to compute the actual guard.

Proof by common-set size. With no common ID the partition leaves V unchanged, so X=Y. With at least two common IDs, union size is at most 2d-2 and the cap retains the whole union. With exactly one common ID, union size is at most 2d-1, hence at most one ID is omitted from P_k. That one common ID appears first; any omitted ID is exclusive to one input. The other complete input is retained. In each case a guard clause is true. This uses full-union construction and stable relative order when identifying the concrete baseline and promoted outputs, and it does not license a grader that ignores later IDs.

Sharpness for every integer d>=2 follows from two lists of length d. Put d-1 private A IDs and d-1 different private B IDs first, then the same common ID last in each. Their alternating union lists the private IDs in A/B order and ends with the common one. At cap 2d-3, RR includes the last private A ID but not the last private B ID. Promotion spends one slot on the common ID and includes neither last private ID. Use those two private singleton IDs as alternatives. Each original input is sufficient, RR completes one alternative, promotion completes none, and the guard rejects. At cap 2d-2, the other complete input is retained and the guard accepts.

The seven d=2..8 saved examples are authored illustrations of that symbolic construction, not seven sampled tasks or external evidence. The proof establishes the all-d statement. For d=0 and d=1, check nonnegative caps directly: empty or singleton inputs cannot create a changed stable order causing a conditional loss. We do not plug d=0 into an expression that yields a negative output capacity.

The result remains no-loss rather than universal success. As a teaching example, take disjoint A=(0,1,2), B=(3,4,5), with alternatives {0,1,2} and {3,4,5}. At cap four both operators select (0,3,1,4), completing neither alternative. Both complete inputs were sufficient. This same logical distinction caused the preserved v19 verifier failure in S12; the current verifier asserts implications rather than success.

sections.heading: S19. Saved gains, conservative rejection and unconditional failure
paragraphs: The saved examples in witnesses.json are actual rows of the existing constructed bank. They are not newly generated model outputs. Task scifact_v4_39 has singleton reference alternatives {7},{8},{9},{10},{11}. With A=(0,7), B=(7), cap one, retaining complete B accepts promotion (7), changing RR failure (0) into success. With A=(7,0), B=(0,8), both inputs contain a reference alternative, but promotion (0) loses RR success (7). Neither full input is retained and sets differ, so the guard falls back and blocks the loss.

The very same policy also preserves an actual loss outside the premise. On scifact_v4_39 with A=(7,0), B=(0), cap one, retention of complete B accepts (0); RR would output (7). Only A is annotation-sufficient. The smallest authored shape of this failure uses A=(0,1), B=(1), reference {0}, as shown in S16-S17. Its union size two, total input length three and cap one are minimal under the finite search ordering stated in PLAN. Minimality is within that declared finite construction, not over all possible agent tasks.

Conservatism is visible on scifact_v4_653. Its singleton alternatives are {0},{1},{5}. With A=(2,0), B=(0,1), cap one, RR selects (2) and fails; promotion selects (0) and passes. Both complete inputs are sufficient, but neither complete input fits the promoted prefix and its set differs from RR. The guard rejects. This is one of the two sacrificed gains. No contradiction follows: a different admissible family using {2} and {1} would make this same shape a promotion loss, so universal safety must reject it.

The last contrast explains why an actual family and a universal class give different answers. We do not alter gold to boost or reduce a measured result: the counterfamily is an authored proof witness, explicitly separate from the stored task references. Its purpose is to show why a reference-blind policy cannot both accept that shape and keep the universal conditional promise. Model-generated text, unannotated semantic validity and skill usefulness need different observables.

sections.heading: S20. Endpoints, cap-dependent switching and weighting
paragraphs: The universal theorem concerns monotone full containment. First-three observes an ordered subprefix, not the equal-cardinality sets compared by G, while exact-annotated can reject a sufficient superset. Each endpoint is recomputed separately for every method. On this bank H has 563/0 first-three gain/loss in the sufficient stratum at cap one, 95/0 at two, 0/0 at three, and 0/2 at four through six. The cap-four losses are not a theorem failure; the evaluator reads a different object.

The first successful capacity for each fixed complete order V or P is its minimum rationale-completion rank, as proved in S4. H is a switch whose choice can change with k. Therefore its outputs are not automatically prefixes of one fixed global order, and the earlier single-window proof must not be imported without checking nestedness. Our new raw rows allow direct cap-by-cap validation and make no universal single-window claim for H.

Weighting describes a different unit of averaging, not a correction that turns constructed multiplicities into natural prevalence. The exact aggregate means stored in results.json are absolute pass rates; a contrast requires subtracting the RR mean with the same weighting. In the sufficient stratum, H pooled cap-one contrast is 563/12067; its equal-component contrast is 124638679619/1757429593920. At cap two they are 95/12067 and 106184173/6051754800 respectively. Their positive signs follow from zero paired full losses here, not from independent evidence.

For unprotected promotion the preserved cap-one sufficient-stratum contrast still reverses sign: pooled -844/12067, equal-component +3363459013/266277211200. All-pair guarded cap-one pooled contrast is only 76/22794, despite 563 gains, because 487 losses remain. sections.heading: S23. Prospective behavioral gates and falsification decisions
paragraphs: The guard proof does not identify a behavioral skill effect because actual skill edits need not preserve a two-input evidence union or satisfy annotation sufficiency. Before moving to agents, admit the task family only if simultaneous requirements are satisfiable, outputs are expressible, verifier rights are allowed, reset is possible, and a meaningful fresh outcome can be observed. Predeclare what counts as a successful individual skill and what is counted when no eligible pair is found. Zero yield is reported as zero eligible pairs and null composition effect, not as proof of safe integration.

Freeze a baseline environment and independently author A/B on D with bounded candidate counts. Q can select or reject proposals under a predeclared improvement gate but cannot silently become training feedback. Freeze selected bytes and the AB order before reserved S. Require equal effective task information, tool privileges, token limits and total proposal/routing/retry/judge accounting across comparison arms. If a native method uses extra context or an assembler, preserve its defining mechanism and charge the additional resource, rather than substituting concatenation and calling it native reproduction.

Use simple RR-like ordering, concatenation, constrained truncation, conservative replay/rejection, typed repair and native routing as distinct comparison rights. A controller that repairs every observed development failure is still a candidate selected on exposed evidence. Component folds diagnose sensitivity; they do not manufacture a new independent S. Fresh behavioral claims need the planned split and arm executions, with failures, deferrals and missingness retained.

Potential falsifiers are concrete. A conditionally sufficient saved pair with H full loss would refute the implementation or theorem assumptions and stop publication. A natural task in which ID retention leaves semantic execution wrong would refute transfer of the contract to that task, without refuting the set theorem. If AB fails only because its requirements conflict, the study must report compatibility failure rather than an interference mechanism. If apparent harm vanishes under a token-matched length control, the narrower capacity explanation wins. If the qualified pair denominator is zero, the targeted behavioral contrast remains undefined.

paper.title: SkillMerge: Agreement, Output Length and the Limits of Compositional Repair
paper.subtitle: From composition diagnostics to agreement, length controls and candidate-class selection
paper.abstract: Can agreement between two useful skill outputs safely guide their composition? We distinguish this unexecuted behavioral question from an exposed SciFact-derived diagnostic bank. V17 retains 309 tasks, 204 components and 22,794 ordered pairs, executes five label-blind output constructors and controls their output lengths. Intersection-only raises exact-reference score against a longer left-union rule but loses sufficient coverage and is worse than a pairwise length-matched uniform subset on both endpoints. An explicitly post-primary controlled audit isolates common-item priority against the same round-robin baseline: zero sufficient gains and two losses, including a saved pair whose two inputs both contain valid alternative rationales. Five component folds always select round-robin for sufficient containment and intersection-only for exact matching, giving no score gain from changing the rule across folds. A gold-aware oracle is only an upper bound for the four predeclared selector candidates; an excluded negative control can exceed it and is not retrospectively promoted. Alternate author implementations verify 113,970 deterministic outputs and 25,119 exact uniform probability cells. All data are already exposed annotation-derived constructions. Independent A/B histories and qualified pairs remain zero and the behavioral composition effect remains null. The contribution is an auditable agreement/selection mechanism comparison with explicit information and cost boundaries. The continuation gives exact capacity-window identities and a conditional no-loss boundary, while first-three truncation and unit weighting retain important failures.
paper.status: Neutral working paper v19, 2026-10-19. New finite saved-evidence diagnostics; no new independent data, real model/API calls, native-method trial or physical acquisition. Previous v17 evidence and v18 presentation are retained.
contributions: A decision-focused formulation of qualified skill composition: joint availability versus the mean isolated branch, conditional on an independently applied qualification gate, with eligibility yield separated from effect.
An executed evidence-contract audit preserving source connectivity, annotation alternatives, exposed-data status, and distinct task/component/response denominators.

Budget-reachability and same-set controls that separate answer-space impossibility, annotation omission, ranking sensitivity, and actual semantic loss; exact finite controls are checked by exhaustive enumeration.

A new executed complete-score-support analysis that turns endpoint disagreements into sharp fixed-cohort contrast-sensitivity envelopes, with separate qualification-cohort transport bounds and explicit worst-case versus behavioral-estimate distinctions.

A falsifiable, equal-information and fully charged comparison protocol against conservative replay, typed migration, and assessment/assembly methods; agent effects remain unestimated rather than inferred from grader diagnostics.

A constrained, fully replayed merge operator exposes a score-sign reversal on the same task cohort, separating monotone evidence union, ranked truncation and exact-set grading without inventing model histories.

An exact order/capacity benchmark with annotation-blind controls, permutation-orbit bounds, a complete sufficient-failure partition and a symmetry counterexample to interpreting local reversal repairs as aggregate improvement.

An executed label-blind agreement audit with pairwise length-matched random controls, component-disjoint rule selection, restricted-class oracle accounting and a post-primary controlled common-priority counterexample.

A new predeclared finite audit keeps the round-robin relative order within common and noncommon IDs and only promotes the common class. For a nested output prefix L, the first sufficient capacity is the minimum, over complete reference alternatives, of the largest reference-ID rank. Two operators therefore differ in sufficiency on at most one contiguous capacity interval for a fixed pair. This is an annotation-containment identity, not a semantic claim about agreeing natural skills.

sections.heading: Introduction
paragraphs: Agent instructions increasingly live in reusable skill files with associated tools and resources. A deployment decision arises when two changes are useful separately: should both become available together, should integration be repaired, or should deployment fall back to an isolated branch? A negative score alone does not answer why integration failed. It could reflect lost evidence, different ordering under a ranked contract, an omitted valid annotation, changed tool rights, or additional context. Distinguishing these possibilities determines which intervention is worth deploying.

Consider an evidence task whose correct rationale contains three sentences. Two isolated configurations and their ancestor return these sentences followed by an irrelevant sentence; the joint configuration returns the same four IDs with the irrelevant one first. A first-three grader reports a strict joint failure, while full-set containment reports no change. If ranked evidence is the application contract, the failure is operationally meaningful. The identical full set nevertheless rules out the stronger explanation that the joint answer lost an annotated evidence sentence. A study that confuses these claims can prescribe the wrong repair.

Our question is therefore two-level. The behavioral target is whether independently qualified changes lose completion jointly. The completed empirical contribution is an audit of the measurement substrate required to investigate that target. This ordering follows established concerns about evidence evaluation [1,3,4] and construct validity [8,9], rather than claiming that measurement validity is newly discovered. The useful gap is operational: a claim about qualified composition needs a chain linking candidate history, held-out qualification, answer expressibility, grader behavior, and fresh deployment outcomes.

We ask three research questions. RQ1: do original valid annotation responses remain accepted, and is a complete answer expressible under the proposed budget? RQ2: which endpoint changes can occur while the full evidence set is fixed? RQ3: what additional histories, controls, and comparison rights are required before estimating a qualified-composition effect? RQ1 and RQ2 receive finite, executed answers; RQ3 receives an explicit prospective protocol. No observation in the completed audit qualifies a skill pair.

The v14 follow-up asks a sharper measurement question: given a task, a response budget and fixed arm outputs, how far could changing the endpoint move the composition contrast? Counting four particular order flips cannot answer that question, because those controls explore only selected responses. We therefore characterize all attainable simultaneous sufficient, first-three and exact scores within a declared response space. A sharp envelope over unrestricted response assignments can be calculated without inventing a single agent history. We also distinguish this same-cohort sensitivity from changing which candidate pairs qualify when the qualification grader changes.

Figure 1 separates these evidential stages. The completed lane contains 531 tasks, 309 evidence-bearing tasks, 548 annotation responses, and 4,186 constructed diagnostics. These are nested units, not independent integration events. The separate behavioral lane has zero authoring histories, zero eligible pairs, and a null effect. Our central practical result is that an incomplete grader and an unexamined response cap would already change eligibility and mechanism interpretations before any model comparison begins.

Figure 1 preserves the earlier measured-versus-prospective separation; Figure 4 adds the new response-space sensitivity analysis. The original 4,186 stored diagnostic rows are not relabeled as new model predictions, and the new abstract score cells are not qualifying events.

V15 asks which measurement patterns survive a concrete coupling between the isolated and merged responses. A union cannot independently choose an arbitrary response for each arm, and cannot invent a new sentence. By replaying that narrow operator we obtain a constructive control below the v14 worst-case envelope: a score decrease can arise from a nonmonotone endpoint even when evidence is preserved, while a capacity-limited union can actually drop the second input's evidence. Both statements can be tested before collecting real skill histories.

V16 then asks whether a visible ranking repair survives a symmetric cohort comparison. Exact prefix-subset enumeration separates reference availability, capacity and order, while annotation-blind controls expose an endpoint tradeoff. The key negative control is that reversing every ordered pair has zero aggregate gain even when it repairs every selected priority failure. Figure 6 links that finite result to the still unexecuted behavioral study.

sections.heading: Related Work
paragraphs: We organize related work by the decision it supports: what counts as evidence, what a benchmark score warrants, and what an integration policy actually does. This avoids treating a dataset, a testing philosophy, and an executable skill-management method as interchangeable performance baselines.

sections.heading: Evidence and rationale evaluation
paragraphs: SciFact evaluates scientific claim–abstract relations with rationale annotations [1]. Its rationalized abstract endpoint uses containment of a complete rationale, whereas its sentence endpoint also penalizes excess predictions. FEVER likewise distinguishes label correctness from evidence-supported correctness and recognizes incomplete evidence annotation [3]. ERASER separates agreement with human rationales from faithfulness to a model's prediction [4]. These distinctions motivate separate endpoints; they do not justify naming exact annotation agreement semantic truth. Our sufficient-containment rule also differs from ERASER's confidence-based notion of rationale sufficiency.

The pinned SciFact implementation slices a supplied rationale list to three IDs for rationalized abstract correctness [2]. The inspected parser retains the supplied list rather than sorting it. We study that local list behavior explicitly. We do not reproduce corpus retrieval, native aggregate precision/recall/F1, or ERASER faithfulness. Original annotations are operational references, not independent domain adjudications.

sections.heading: Behavioral testing and warranted inference
paragraphs: CheckList distinguishes focused functionality, invariance, and directional tests [5]. Our same-set controls apply this testing logic to deterministic graders, not to a model evaluated through CheckList. HELM motivates examining several desiderata in the same scenarios [6]; BIG-bench discusses sensitivity to task and metric specification [7]. Construct-validity analyses make the score-to-claim assumptions explicit [8,9]. We implement a narrow part of that agenda through executable acceptance and answer-space checks.

Underspecification warns that similar held-out predictive performance can coexist with different deployment behavior [11]. Datasheets motivate explicit composition, collection, and intended-use documentation [12], while The Benchmark Lottery motivates fixing task selection and weighting rather than interpreting a convenient ranking as universal [13]. None proves that a particular skill pair interferes. Together they explain why our exposed annotation audit supports an engineering admission decision but not a behavioral population estimate.

sections.heading: Skill evolution and integration controls
paragraphs: DSPy compiles modular language-model programs against an explicit metric, including metric-filtered traces [10]. SkillCommit emphasizes source-case replay and conservative scope management [14]. SkillSmith includes typed operations and required caller updates [15]. SkillCAT v2 uses assessment with an LLM router and an LLM assembler [16]. SkillEvoReg studies candidate-conditioned regression validation and repair [17]. These provide substantive comparison mechanisms, but optimize or condition on different objects; none is automatically an estimator of our qualified-pair contrast.

Signal or Noise separates skill instructions, matched irrelevant content, slices, and mounted resources [18]. Its byte-matched control motivates a length diagnostic, while actual tokenizer equality remains a separate requirement. SkillsBench's versioned task/environment/oracle/verifier packages offer a prospective workflow setting [19]. We inspect these primary sources and specify comparison rights; we execute none of their native systems, import none of their reported scores, and make no priority claim over their broader mechanisms.

sections.heading: Problem Formulation and Method
paragraphs: An event fixes a common skill ancestor S0, two branch changes A and B, their associated resource graph, and a canonical joint configuration AB. Installation, routing, actual reading, and runtime assembly are distinct interventions. The primary behavioral treatment is joint availability under a declared deployment policy. A forced-activation test can diagnose a route, but cannot replace availability while retaining the same estimand.

sections.heading: Qualification-conditioned target
paragraphs: Authors may use development information D but cannot inspect each other's change or auditor-only Q/S labels. An event qualifies only if both isolated branches satisfy a predeclared gain rule against the same ancestor on Q. Qualification must be based on observed task behavior, not an assigned role or a critic's approval. Proposal caps, duplicate attempts, authoring failures, and Q failures remain in a yield ledger. Selection on Q defines a conditional target; it does not measure the frequency of harmful merges among all proposed changes.

For a qualified event and task, p0, pA, pB, and pAB denote completion probabilities under fresh reset executions with fixed model identity, rights, contract, and accounting. The primary contrast compares joint deployment to an equal mixture of isolated branches. It does not select the best branch after inspecting final S. Weights over histories and source families must be declared before S; task-rich components otherwise receive unintended extra influence.

The interaction tau is different. The authored cell (S0,A,B,AB)=(0,1,1,1) gives tau=-1 but primary contrast zero: joint deployment is not worse than either isolated branch. A strict cell (1,1,1,0), a negative mean contrast, and a high-probability witness are also different claims. The current ledger contains no actual A/B histories, Q evaluations, or assigned S cells; all composition effects and witness incidence remain null.
equations: tau_(e,t) = p_(A B) - p_A - p_B + p_0

sections.heading: Evidence contracts
paragraphs: For an evidence-bearing task t, let its n sentence IDs be stable and let R1 through Rm be its original nonempty rationale sets. A response L is an ordered list of distinct in-range IDs. Every executed diagnostic receives the correct label from the auditor. This isolates evidence-contract behavior and deliberately excludes label prediction. Insufficient tasks use a separate explicit label and empty evidence in the local adapter.

Unlimited sufficiency accepts when a complete original rationale occurs anywhere in the response set. First-three applies containment only to the first three supplied IDs. Exact-annotated accepts when the full set equals an enumerated rationale. An intentionally incomplete first-annotation-only comparator retains only the first original rationale. The last comparator tests omission and is never proposed as an admissible deployed grader. Order invariance, tolerance of extra evidence, and preservation of alternatives are distinct properties.

The endpoint must follow the application. Containment can reward an answer with excessive unrelated material; exact matching can reject a valid unannotated explanation. Ranked evidence may be a legitimate retrieval requirement. We therefore audit contracts without promoting whichever endpoint makes a preferred composition story appear. The local cited-document task and its insufficient convention differ from native SciFact retrieval and aggregate scoring [1,2].

sections.heading: Reachability, invariance, and exact controls
paragraphs: Proposition 1. Under an at-most-k sentence budget, an annotated sufficient answer exists if and only if the shortest original rationale has size at most k. Necessity follows because a response containing a complete rationale cannot be shorter than that rationale. Sufficiency follows by returning the shortest rationale itself. This is an answer-space condition, not a model success bound conditional on arbitrary generation behavior. A first-three cap consequently makes any task with only longer rationales unreachable under that endpoint.

Proposition 2. Full-set containment is invariant to permutations of L and monotone under adding IDs. Exact-annotated is permutation invariant but need not be monotone. First-three need not be permutation invariant. For a three-ID rationale R and an ID d outside every annotated rationale, compare [r1,r2,r3,d] with [d,r1,r2,r3]. Their full sets are identical and sufficient, but only the first passes first-three. Assigning the first list to S0/A/B and the second to AB constructs a strict score cell without losing any full-set evidence. This is a deterministic counterexample, not an eligible behavioral event.

A uniform k-subset control quantifies document-position structure without inventing predictions. With k=min(b,n), inclusion–exclusion over nonempty subsets J of distinct rationales gives the exact probability that the chosen set contains at least one rationale. Here uJ is the size of their union; impossible binomial terms are zero. Exact-annotated instead counts distinct size-k annotations divided by the total number of size-k subsets. Exact rational arithmetic and exhaustive checks avoid Monte Carlo uncertainty. These elementary results are useful contract checks, not claims of mathematical priority.
equations: q_(t,k) = sum_(J != emptyset) (-1)^(|J|+1) frac(binom(n_t-u_J, k-u_J), binom(n_t,k))

sections.heading: When endpoint disagreement changes a composition contrast
paragraphs: Endpoint disagreement alone does not determine the direction of a composition effect. Hold the qualified cohort Q, task weights, and arm outputs fixed, and let eta_z be the expected difference between two binary graders g and h on arm z. Linearity gives the contrast decomposition below. If every arm has the same discrepancy, it cancels. A task that is unreachable under one contract for all arms therefore imposes a ceiling but need not create a negative joint-minus-isolated contrast. Its effect on qualification or weighting is a separate question.

If epsilon_z is the weighted probability that the graders disagree on arm z within that same fixed Q cohort, the triangle inequality yields the displayed sensitivity bound. These are conditional algebraic statements, not numerical estimates from our oracle diagnostics. We have no arm-specific model outputs, so neither eta nor epsilon is observed for a qualified composition population. In particular, 239 omitted-alternative rejections and four constructed order flips cannot be substituted into the bound as model disagreement probabilities.

Changing the grader used for Q may also change which histories qualify. Then even the cohort differs, and the fixed-Q identity cannot transport one reported effect to the other without additional assumptions or observations. A future study should distinguish rescoring the same frozen S outputs from rerunning qualification under a different contract. The former diagnoses measurement sensitivity; the latter changes the conditional study population. This distinction prevents treating a convenient endpoint switch as either a repaired mechanism or evidence of general collapse.
equations: theta_Q^(g) - theta_Q^(h) = E_w[eta_(A B) - frac(eta_A+eta_B,2) mid Q=1]

sections.heading: Complete score support and sharp fixed-cohort envelopes
paragraphs: For this follow-up, an admissible response is an ordered list of distinct, in-range sentence IDs of length at most k, including the empty list. Labels are auditor-correct. Let U, T and E denote sufficient, first-three and exact-annotated scoring. Both T and E imply U, so only five binary patterns can occur: (0,0,0), (1,0,0), (1,0,1), (1,1,0) and (1,1,1). The response-support algorithm records a minimum-length witness for every attainable pattern, not merely patterns observed in a few prefix controls.

Every current task has a sentence ID outside the union of all enumerated rationale sets. This is checked rather than assumed for an arbitrary future benchmark. Exact responses are the original rationale sets with each relevant three-ID prefix. A short rationale followed by that outside-union ID supplies a sufficient/first-three but nonexact witness. To complete the remaining sufficient-but-not-first-three and nonexact pattern, enumerate unsuccessful three-ID prefixes and complete an original rationale after them. If their union is exact, append the outside-union ID. The appendix proves that any longer admissible witness can be reduced to one of these constructions without increasing its length.

For endpoints g and h and a fixed task t, let the discrepancy be g(L)-h(L). Its minimum and maximum over admissible responses define a taskwise range. With nonnegative fixed task weights summing to one, the sharp symmetric envelope for the change in joint-minus-mean-isolated contrast is the weighted mean of those ranges. Choose the joint response at the maximum discrepancy and both isolated responses at the minimum to attain the upper endpoint; reverse them for the lower endpoint. Sharpness is relative to unrestricted deterministic response assignments independently chosen for each arm and task. It does not assert that any qualified skill or learning procedure can generate the extremizer.

This support envelope refines the earlier disagreement-probability inequality when only endpoint structure is known. For nested binary graders, discrepancies have one sign and the taskwise range is at most one, rather than the unconstrained two. First-three and exact are not generally nested. In a five-ID authored example with rationales (0) and (0,1,2,3), responses (0,4) and (1,2,3,0) have discrepancies +1 and -1. Assigning them to opposite arms attains a contrast change of two. No task in the current data has that two-sided pattern support. Dataset-specific absence must not become a universal nesting claim.
equations: R_w^(g h)(k) = sum_t w_t (M_t^(g h)(k)-m_t^(g h)(k))
