sections.heading: Changing qualification is a separate transport problem
paragraphs: A qualification grader can change the target cohort as well as final-output scores. To make the distinction executable, we exhaust an illustrative one-task binary gate: both isolated responses must strictly outperform the same ancestor. Every ancestor/A/B score cell uses a feasible response pattern. The resulting counts identify tasks on which a gate change is possible, not the frequency of changes among real proposals and not the study's eventual multi-task qualification rule. Even when g never scores a response below h, the gate can move in either direction: g may upgrade a weak isolated branch or upgrade the ancestor and eliminate its measured gain.

For a common original cohort measure and unchanged history weights, let q_g and q_h be the masses admitted by two nonempty gates and r their intersection mass. The total variation distance between the two normalized selected distributions is one minus r divided by the larger admission mass. A mean-isolated contrast lies in [-1,1], so changing only that selected distribution can move its expectation by at most twice this distance. This is a finite algebraic transport bound, not an assumption that the two gates admit equal histories.

Decompose a full grader-and-gate switch through the h score on the g cohort. The first term is same-cohort rescoring and admits the support envelope; the second is cohort transport and admits the total-variation bound. Their sum can be capped by two because the two reported contrasts lie in [-1,1]. This comparison requires fixed candidates, common base weights, and enough retained final-output support to define the bridge quantity. If access rights, authoring behavior or final executions change, those are additional interventions. If either qualification cohort is empty, its conditional effect and this transport comparison are undefined and remain null. Current gate memberships, admission masses and overlap are unobserved; no numerical transport correction is applied to a behavioral effect.

sections.heading: Experimental Setup
paragraphs: The completed experiments operate on public dataset records and authored oracle-label response lists. The earlier audit establishes source reconstruction and basic grader behavior; the follow-up measurement run adds budget, alternative, same-set, and combinatorial diagnostics. The present revision adds analysis and inspected literature, not another predictive experiment.

sections.heading: Sources, splitting, and exposure
paragraphs: The preserved raw snapshot contains 809 training claims, 300 development claims, and 5,183 abstracts. An independent breadth-first reconstruction checks the prepared adapter against raw bytes, including original labels and rationale alternatives. Excluding 278 training claims linked to development sources leaves 531 local tasks in 325 structural components. Of these, 309 evidence-bearing tasks occupy 204 components; 222 are insufficient tasks. These are local adapter counts, not a substituted official benchmark population.

Recorded cross-split component, selected-document, and normalized-claim overlaps are zero under the reconstruction rules. Structural separation is narrower than semantic independence or pretraining-contamination freedom. All 531 selected labels and annotations were already exposed during development audit. None is a blind final set for a newly authored skill. The exposure ledger follows the documentation rationale of [12], but no documentation artifact itself guarantees independence.

The rationale family has 548 original annotation records across 309 evidence tasks. Task-level shortest-rationale sizes are one on 290 tasks, two on 15, three on three, and four on one. Across all annotation records, the corresponding counts are 510, 33, four, and one. Alternatives share tasks and sources; treating 548 responses as independent tasks would change the denominator without adding independent evidence.

sections.heading: Diagnostic construction and validation
paragraphs: For each original annotation we construct its ordered IDs with the correct label. For each budget from one through ten we also return a document prefix of at most that many IDs. Reachability is computed independently of this prefix policy. Finally, for every annotation, we choose one sentence outside the union of its task's annotated rationales and place the same ID before versus after the annotation. All 309 evidence tasks support this construction; no task is silently excluded. The full set, label, and distractor identity are fixed within a pair.

The saved run contains 4,186 diagnostic rows. Basic scorer checks include original annotation/empty responses, wrong labels, evidence deletions, and malformed outputs from the preceding audit. Follow-up mathematical checks cover overlapping and duplicate rationale families as well as boundary budgets. Saved traces are reaggregated and their input/output byte bindings checked; all 66,431 real-data size-three subsets are exhaustively enumerated to verify the analytic control. This establishes specified software relationships, not label correctness or independent scientific replication.

No model, router, assembler, or tool-using agent produces these responses. The execution makes zero model calls and zero network requests. Later literature HTML retrieval belongs to this revision's source review, not to the offline experiment. We preserve the executed plan, script snapshot, results, row traces, and receipts, including an explicit supplement for a prepared-manifest binding omitted from the original follow-up receipt.

sections.heading: New finite support analysis and checks
paragraphs: One new offline run freezes the analysis code, plan, task measurements, prior diagnostics, prior result and prior byte receipt before support analysis. It uses all 309 evidence tasks in 204 structural components, with all 548 rationale alternatives. All labels were already development-exposed. The empty response is an explicit failure response in the at-most-budget contract, rather than a new semantic annotation. This follows the earlier correct-label endpoint definitions; it is not native SciFact aggregate evaluation.

We compare certificate support against complete ordered-response enumeration for all 127 nonempty rationale families on three evidence IDs plus a fourth outside-union ID: 16,256 score checks. All 152 real tasks with at most eight sentence IDs receive independent response-set/prefix enumeration at budgets one through four, giving 608 task-budget support comparisons. The preserved 4,186 diagnostic rows expand to 4,734 response instances because order-pair rows contain two responses; all three endpoint scores are independently recalculated. The main analysis checks 460,020 feasible three-arm score cells and attains both signed envelope extrema. These are dependent software checks on a fixed collection, not independent model trials.

A separate verifier checks byte bindings, rescores 1,222 stored minimum-length support witnesses, and recomputes all 30 aggregate rows. Because the small-family universe cannot contain a four-sentence rationale, it separately brute-forces the actual unique four-sentence task at budgets three, four and five. Five adversarial rationale families add 3,250 ordered-response checks, including mixed short/long annotations with two-sided first-three/exact discrepancy. All checks pass. The main finite analysis took approximately 0.88 seconds in this local execution; this is bookkeeping, not a controlled efficiency comparison.

sections.heading: Results and Analysis
paragraphs: Results answer admission and interpretation questions on a fixed exposed corpus. Exact counts require no sampling interval for this corpus; they do not estimate a population composition rate. We retain endpoint-specific denominators and distinguish existential reachability from achieved diagnostic scores.

sections.heading: Budget changes expressibility before behavior
paragraphs: Figure 2 plots the answer-space ceiling and the constructed prefix policy on the same 309 tasks. Budgets one, two, three, and four permit a complete annotated answer on 290, 305, 308, and 309 tasks respectively. The unique four-sentence-only annotation remains preserved; a three-ID endpoint cannot accept it even with perfect sentence selection. A historical paper description of rationale length does not replace checking the actual raw snapshot and adapter.

Document-prefix sufficient passes rise from 17 at budget one to 76 at three, 119 at four, and 251 at ten. First-three passes plateau at 76 after budget three. Exact-annotated prefix passes are 17, three, and zero at budgets one, two, and three; they remain zero through ten. These curves measure different contracts, not a model becoming worse at verification as its budget increases. Under exact matching, extra predicted IDs can change a previously exact set into a rejection by definition.

This changes an immediate design decision: either preserve the ranking cap and explicitly account for unreachable original cases, or define a justified adapted task before testing new behavior. Silently discarding the four-sentence case or increasing the cap after observing a desired effect would change the target. We make neither change and promote no endpoint.

figures.caption: Sentence budgets 1–10 on the same 309 evidence-bearing tasks. Annotation reachability is an existential answer-space ceiling, while prefix sufficient/first-three/exact curves score constructed document-prefix responses with auditor-correct labels. At k=3, 308 tasks are reachable but only 76 prefix responses pass sufficient containment; the first-three curve then plateaus. These are not LLM accuracies.

sections.heading: Alternative preservation and same-set order effects
paragraphs: Every original annotation response passes unlimited sufficiency and exact-annotated: 548/548 each. First-three accepts 547/548. The incomplete first-annotation-only comparator accepts 309/548, losing 239 original valid annotation responses, or 43.61% of these response units. This is not a 43.61-point model gain: the same task can contribute several alternatives, and no model chose among them. It is a concrete reason to reject that incomplete grader for the stated annotation-preserving contract.

Figure 3 compares original responses with the same one-distractor set in two orders. Unlimited sufficiency accepts 548/548 in both orders. First-three accepts 543/548 when the distractor is prepended and 547/548 when appended, producing four paired flips. Exact-annotated rejects every distractor response in both orders because the chosen ID lies outside every rationale. The incomplete comparator accepts 309 in either order. Four flips are an observed count among constructed annotation pairs, not the natural incidence of harmful merges.

The control rules out full-set evidence loss as an explanation for these particular flips. It does not invalidate ranking as a task requirement, nor does it establish that model attention, instruction conflict, or context length caused a behavioral change. Those require model-produced outputs and matched interventions. An integration policy whose only benefit is moving evidence into a required prefix may be useful, but its claim should name ranking repair.

figures.caption: Pass counts for 548 original annotation responses, nested in 309 tasks, under four contracts. Original/prepend/append counts are 548/548/548 for unlimited sufficiency, 547/543/547 for first-three, 548/0/0 for exact-annotated, and 309/309/309 for the deliberately incomplete first-annotation-only control. Prepend/append hold the full set fixed; their four first-three flips are constructed diagnostics, not composition incidence.

sections.heading: Finite controls and the missing behavioral denominator
paragraphs: At size three, uniform-subset sufficient containment has exact equal-task expectation 0.490307, compared with document-prefix containment 76/309, approximately 0.245955. This diagnoses sentence-position structure under correct labels; it does not show a random agent outperforming a verification model. Equal-component averaging yields 0.496126, numerically different because tasks and components induce different targets. Reporting one as the other would hide a weighting choice.

The authored formula passes 165 exhaustive small-family comparisons and five additional contract-check groups. Independent saved-trace validation reaggregates all 4,186 rows, checks 25 bound input/output files, and confirms the real-data three-subset enumeration. The elementary propositions and diagnostic counts are consequently supported as finite software/data statements, conditional on the annotations and definitions.

The behavioral funnel remains empty: actual A/B histories=0, Q-evaluated pairs=0, eligible pairs=0, and assigned S cells=0. Theta_Q, interaction, and strict-witness rate are null. The nulls mean missing behavioral evidence, not zero harm. Neither successful software tests nor a model critic's agreement can populate those denominators.

sections.heading: Response-space sensitivity is not observed disagreement incidence
paragraphs: Figure 4 reports the new support-envelope radii. At budgets one through three, sufficient and first-three give identical scores for every admissible response, so their fixed-cohort contrast difference is exactly zero. At budget four, 296 of 309 tasks support both zero and positive sufficient-minus-first-three discrepancy. Their equal-task radius is 296/309, approximately 0.957929, and it remains unchanged through budget ten. Equal-component weighting yields approximately 0.967320. The 13 remaining tasks have no such score variation in this response space. A large worst-case radius means annotation and endpoint structure alone cannot guarantee sign robustness; it does not mean models usually approach this extremum.

Sufficient versus exact has equal-task radii zero at budget one, 290/309 at two, 305/309 at three, 308/309 at four, and one from five onward. The unique four-sentence rationale is exact at four IDs and becomes a sufficient but nonexact response when an extra ID is permitted at five. First-three versus exact has radius 305/309 at budget three and one from four onward. All current taskwise radii are zero or one, although the adversarial family demonstrates that radius two is possible on a different annotation structure.

These results explain why the earlier four particular one-distractor order flips cannot be used as an overall error probability or sensitivity bound. Those controls expose four changes within their selected paired responses; complete response support allows other scored prefixes with no annotated rationale followed by a valid rationale. Conversely, zero sufficient/first-three sensitivity at budget three does not validate that budget: the earlier audit shows one original task whose four-sentence-only answer is unreachable for both graders. Agreement between endpoints can coexist with a common answer-space failure.

The envelope is calculated on the exposed development collection with declared weights. It is not R_Q for an unknown qualified population and cannot be substituted for theta_Q. A future same-output score rescoring can use its own arm-specific disagreements, which may cancel and be much smaller than the worst-case support radius. A future negative contrast is sign-robust only if its uncertainty and declared endpoint-sensitivity allowance support that conclusion. No such behavioral estimate or uncertainty interval exists in the current study.

Each curve is the sharp equal-task radius of endpoint-induced change in joint-minus-mean-isolated contrast, conditional on correct labels, at-most-k distinct sentence IDs, fixed task weights and unrestricted per-arm response assignment. Sufficient/first-three is zero through k=3 and 296/309 from k=4. Sufficient/exact reaches one at k=5; first-three/exact reaches one at k=4. Curves are worst-case envelopes, not model effects or error frequencies.

sections.heading: Nested graders do not make qualification changes one-sided
paragraphs: At budget four, the illustrative single-task gate can admit under sufficient but not first-three on 296 tasks; it can admit under first-three but not sufficient on 295 tasks. These are overlapping task-level possibility counts, not observed gate outcomes or two groups of candidate histories. The asymmetry comes from the four-sentence-only task: first-three never accepts an admissible answer there, so it cannot qualify an improvement under that gate. Thus responsewise leniency does not imply selectionwise leniency. Any study that changes the Q grader must retain admission and overlap denominators, not merely rescore final S on the original selected cohort.

For the real target, no authoring histories, Q evaluations, eligible pairs or assigned S cells exist. The actual Q overlap, behavioral endpoint-disagreement frequencies and composition effects stay null. The useful new result is the exact separation between what endpoint structure can certify and what only a candidate-history experiment can identify.

sections.heading: Constrained union-replay protocol
paragraphs: The unrestricted v14 response-space radius permits any admissible deterministic output per arm. It does not describe a learned merger or impose a realizability relation between A, B and AB. We now impose one explicit relation: AB is the ordered deduplicated union of A followed by previously unseen IDs from B. A second operator returns only that union's first three IDs. Neither is a model or a skill implementation; they are mechanistic controls for what a measurement can call a failure.

We freeze the prior task_measurements.json and diagnostic_rows.jsonl before execution. Every explicit ids, append_ids and prepend_ids field is inspected. The 4,734 explicit responses include oracle original annotations and deliberately constructed diagnostics. Within each task we deduplicate ordered responses and retain only responses of length at most three. This yields 2,494 unique input responses on all 309 evidence-bearing tasks in 204 structural components; no task has an empty retained bank. The restriction deliberately excludes a four-sentence-only original rationale as an isolated full answer. It is an expressibility constraint, not a successful qualification decision.

All ordered pairs from each task's retained bank are replayed, including A=B and both A,B versus B,A. There are 22,794 pairs and 45,588 operator applications. Ordered pairs are necessary because a ranked-capacity merger prioritizes A. Identical pairs remain because idempotence is part of the declared control. Pair multiplicities are diagnostic design choices, not sampled model-use frequencies. The pair-pooled denominator and the equal-task estimand are therefore reported separately.

For each endpoint we compute merged score minus the arithmetic mean of the two isolated scores. The primary summary averages first over every task's ordered pairs and then equally over 309 tasks. An equal-component result first averages task summaries inside each of the 204 components. Pair pooling weights tasks with a larger retained response bank more heavily and is a sensitivity summary rather than a replacement for the primary aggregation.

Input labels are auditor-correct throughout. Each isolated input has at most three sentence IDs; untruncated union can have six, whereas prefix3 has at most three. Thus an untruncated gain is not evidence of superiority at identical output cost. The analysis fixes task identity and label correctness, not realized tokens, model inference or context usage. No Q score or candidate history is generated.

sections.heading: Monotone evidence can receive a negative exact-match contrast
paragraphs: An untruncated union contains every evidence ID returned by either input. Under the sufficient endpoint, any accepted input rationale is therefore still present. We verify zero losses relative to either input on every pair. Nevertheless exact matching is nonmonotone: when A and B contain different individually valid rationale alternatives, their union may equal no original annotation set. Original alternatives [0] and [1] provide the minimal counterexample: both isolated answers are exact, while union [0,1] is sufficient but nonexact.

The executed equal-task union contrast is +0.199744 for sufficient, +0.136890 for first-three and -0.179878 for exact. Equal-component values are +0.198667, +0.136938 and -0.178035, so the sign reversal does not disappear under that declared regrouping. Pair-pooled values are +0.185838, +0.129815 and -0.206414. These are three different weighting summaries of the same diagnostic objects, not independent replications.

Exact grading produces 700 ordered pairs whose two isolated responses pass but merged union fails; sufficiency produces zero. Exact union also falls below at least one input in 8,718 pairs. A negative exact contrast is operationally real if exact annotation equality is the task contract. It is insufficient evidence that evidence content was lost, since every merged output is verified to contain both input sets. We do not redefine exact failure away; we restrict its mechanism interpretation.

The union never beats both isolated responses under sufficiency in this retained bank. Its positive contrast comes from cases with one successful and one unsuccessful input, not observed complementary partial rationales becoming a full answer. This negative coverage fact matters: the existing diagnostic construction does not span every behavior a real merger might exhibit. No frequency in this bank estimates the probability of such complementarity in model outputs.

figures.caption: New v15 deterministic response coupling. Ordered union has positive sufficient and negative exact-grading contrast on the same fixed task bank. Prefix3 exposes ranked capacity loss. All values condition on correct labels and constructed responses; no observed model interaction or independent sample claim.

sections.heading: Capacity and input order are distinct interventions
paragraphs: Prefix3 sufficiency exactly equals first-three union scoring on every pair, producing equal-task contrast +0.136890. Compared with untruncated sufficient union, capacity reduces that diagnostic contrast by 0.062854. This is an operator comparison over identical inputs, not a confidence interval or an inferred natural loss rate. The explicit full outputs distinguish actual sentence omission under truncation from mere endpoint rejection under exact grading.

There are 1,277 ordered pairs for which first-three union, equivalently sufficient prefix3, scores below at least one input. No pair loses when both inputs pass, because the A-prioritizing operator preserves all of A's at-most-three IDs. This asymmetry is built into the operator and explains why a both-pass criterion alone misses loss of an individually useful B when A fails. Both A,B and B,A are included so that this chosen prioritization remains visible.

One counterexample has A=[0,1,2], B=[3], with original rationale [3]. Ordered union preserves the rationale, its first-three score fails and a prefix3 output actually omits ID3. Reversing the inputs places ID3 first and avoids that particular capacity failure. In contrast, reordering a union containing two distinct exact alternatives cannot make its full set exact. A repair aimed at ranking and a repair aimed at the acceptance contract therefore address different causal constructions.

We independently recompute all 136,764 pair-by-endpoint/operator cells without importing the author scorer, checking all 1,854 task summaries and both-pass rejection counts. Idempotence, no invented IDs, distinct-ID caps, sufficient monotonicity and the exact/truncation counterexamples are executable assertions. These calculations validate the finite replay implementation on exposed annotations; they do not validate an authoring system or establish independent data.

The next behavioral experiment must keep the union and prefix controls as declared baselines, preserve every initiated authoring history, qualify A and B using Q without S feedback and evaluate all arms on S with explicit costs. Until those histories exist, actual_A_B_histories=0, eligible_pair_n=0 and the qualified interaction effect remains null. A response-bank replay cannot silently fill that denominator.

sections.heading: Exact order and capacity diagnostics
paragraphs: The v15 prefix counterexample leaves a tempting but incomplete prescription: reverse the two inputs. That repairs a chosen example, but what happens when every ordered pair is retained? We make this intervention explicit before claiming a better integration strategy. The research question now holds the available sentence set fixed and distinguishes a missing reference rationale, a rationale too large for the declared output, and a rationale that could fit but is excluded by one ordering.

The new plan and code are frozen with the exact earlier task measurements, diagnostic rows and v15 result before execution. We retain all 2,494 distinct at-most-three-ID input responses, all 309 evidence tasks, all 204 structural components and all 22,794 ordered pairs, including identical pairs. This continuation reuses exposed oracle-authored diagnostics. It makes 638,232 deterministic output replays across four controls and seven capacities; these are not new model predictions or independent behavioral trials.

Left union, right union, ascending document IDs and round-robin interleaving see only A and B. Each deduplicates the same union U and emits its first min(c,|U|) distinct IDs for capacities c=0 through6. Round robin interleaves A0,B0,A1,B1 and so on before deduplication; document order uses numeric sentence position rather than a relevance oracle. All controls therefore share the same available information and output-ID count for a given pair and capacity. Equal IDs do not imply equal tokens, inference cost, content quality or runtime.

For a uniform permutation of U, every size-k prefix subset is equally likely, where k=min(c,|U|). We enumerate these subsets rather than sample seeds. Sufficient and exact expectations use k; the first-three endpoint uses min(c,3,|U|). For every endpoint we also calculate the smallest and largest score over the orbit. Those extrema use annotations and belong only to the auditor. No policy receives the successful prefix or a gold-derived ordering.

The primary estimand is the equal-task mean score, averaging declared pairs within each task first. Equal-component and pair-pooled means remain separate sensitivities. We report score levels rather than silently changing the isolated-arm capacity in a new interaction contrast. The new code separately reproduces every one of the six v15 contrasts under its original alone-response contract. No endpoint is renamed as ERASER confidence-based sufficiency or an official SciFact leaderboard score [1,2,4].
equations: P_("suff")(U,c) = frac("successful size-k subsets of U", "all size-k subsets of U")
P_("exact")(U,c) = frac("size-k reference alternatives contained in U", "all size-k subsets of U")

sections.heading: A disjoint failure diagnosis and its reference boundary
paragraphs: For a failed sufficient left-prefix score, first ask whether any supplied reference rationale is contained in the full union. If none is, classify information_unavailable. Otherwise ask whether at least one contained rationale has size at most min(c,|U|). If none fits, classify capacity_unreachable. Every remaining failure is order_contingent. A success is the fourth class. This sequence makes the failure categories disjoint and exhaustive without claiming access to latent semantic correctness.

At capacity three, left-union sufficient failures divide into 2,255 pairs with no reference rationale anywhere in the available union, zero with a present but unfit rationale, and 1,277 with a fitting rationale excluded by the chosen order. These three classes plus 19,262 successful pairs exhaust all 22,794 pairs. The partition is conditional on the supplied reference alternatives: unavailability here is not a proof that the source text lacks other semantically valid evidence. A failed score therefore determines different next checks depending on whether information, capacity or ordering is implicated.

At capacity one the same partition contains 2,255 information-unavailable, 871 capacity-unreachable and 9,630 order-contingent failures, plus 10,038 passes. At capacity two only 28 capacity-unreachable cases remain. At capacities four and five there are still 67 and three left-priority ordering failures. Full capacity six removes every ordering failure but leaves the same 2,255 unavailable-reference cases. Thus neither adding a slot nor reranking can supply a reference rationale absent from both inputs.

The cap-three permutation orbit contains 2,574 pairs whose sufficient score changes under some ordering, whereas exchanging only source priority gives 2,554 sufficient disagreements. Merely testing two source orders is therefore not a complete permutation-invariance test. Exact matching has only 28 order-contingent pairs at that capacity and becomes order-invariant from capacity four in this bank. It can still fail because the final set contains extras; absence of ordering sensitivity is not acceptance.

sections.heading: A local reversal repair has zero symmetric-cohort gain
paragraphs: All 1,277 v15 losses below a passing input at capacity three are repaired by putting B first. That statement conditions on a failure selected after its score is known. Across the complete ordered cohort, swapping A and B is a bijection: the right-priority output for (A,B) equals the left-priority output for (B,A). Their sums are therefore exactly equal within every task, endpoint and capacity. Equal-task and equal-component aggregation preserve equality. A visible repair gallery cannot establish an aggregate advantage if its symmetric regressions are omitted.

The cap-three sufficient score is 0.791700 for either source priority, 0.728582 for ascending IDs, 0.838328 for round robin and 0.814469 for exact uniform expectation. The annotation-aware lower and upper mean bounds are 0.727773 and 0.854553. Oracle knowledge must not be credited as a comparator's allowed information. The observed round-robin improvement is a finite property of this constructed bank, not a selected or independently tested agent intervention.

The endpoint tradeoff remains visible. At the same cap three, round robin lowers exact-reference mean from 0.031134 to 0.029119; the uniform expectation is 0.029697. A reordering that helps containment can hurt exact equality. The contained-reference sufficient probability is nondecreasing as capacity grows; exact-match probability need not be. For a four-ID union with one singleton rationale, the exact probability is one quarter at capacity one and zero at three. A scalar 'merge quality' claim would conceal that contract change.

A stronger universal-order claim is also false without annotations. Keep identical observed inputs A=[0], B=[1] and capacity one, but consider two otherwise admissible task worlds with reference [0] versus [1]. Any deterministic annotation-blind output is the same in both worlds and fails in one. The counterexample is a constructed information limitation, not a new SciFact instance or a frequency estimate. A method can exploit task text or learned scores, but then those additional rights and their costs must be declared and evaluated.

sections.heading: Benchmark alignment, reproducibility and the next behavioral gate
paragraphs: We reopened the official SciFact record and pinned evaluator source [1,2]. Its inspected abstract-level correctness checks document and label, then tests containment after slicing the supplied rationale list to three sentences. The local first-three endpoint conditions on correct labels and a supplied document; capacities above three and full exact-set equality are explicit diagnostic adaptations. We did not run retrieval, document selection, the native model baseline or official aggregate precision/recall. Comparison to a public SciFact system would require restoring those tasks and the exact split and scorer contract.

ERASER's original HTML separates agreement with human rationales from faithfulness to a model's prediction [4]. Our containment orbit studies the former kind of reference dependence; it does not measure how the evidence influenced an actual model. CheckList motivates focused behavior tests [5], but no CheckList package or language-model suite was run. We also reopened the pinned SkillsBench v1.1 release [19]: its native environment, oracle and verifier packages support a possible workflow-level follow-up. Reading its release is not an executed benchmark, and a skill/no-skill contrast alone does not supply independently qualified A/B composition.

Author-written verification avoids importing the analyzed scorer. Inclusion-exclusion over contained rationale events and direct alternative-size counting check 74,445 orbit probability cells. Full permutations for one union orbit of every observed size 0–6 check 6,111 prefix evaluations. A second direct reconstruction checks 1,914,696 deterministic endpoint cells, all 22,794 pairs, all 147 aggregate rows and the 1,277 reversals. This is a distinct computation by the same author on the same exposed inputs. Nonauthor review, complete manuscript checks and any future empirical replication must be recorded separately.

The finite order benchmark does not add a single independent authoring history. Actual A/B histories and independently qualified pairs remain zero, and the qualified behavioral effect remains null. Plan, code and input locks make a development computation inspectable; they do not undo prior exposure or establish that a real skill merger follows any declared sentence operator. A behavioral claim still requires complete initiated histories, Q-only qualification without S feedback, fresh S arm outputs and fully charged comparison rights.

The next admissible behavioral benchmark should keep union, prefix3, round-robin and a simple randomized order as frozen controls on the same saved real arm outputs. It must specify document/label rights, returned IDs and actual tokenizer costs, retain failures and all started authoring attempts, and use an independently reserved S cohort after Q-only qualification. An annotation-aware permutation envelope can then diagnose a measured loss without being mistaken for the deployed repair. A success criterion must be declared before the new S outcomes are exposed.

sections.heading: Agreement as a policy signal
paragraphs: V16 shows that a local input reversal can repair selected failures without improving the reversal-symmetric cohort. V17 asks a different operational question: can common evidence IDs supply a useful, label-blind composition signal? We keep the same 309 tasks, 204 recorded components, 2,494 inputs and 22,794 ordered pairs. Each constructor receives A and B only. Reference labels enter evaluation and training-component rule selection, never the output constructor. This remains an exposed diagnostic bank rather than independently authored skill behavior.

Let U be the distinct union, I its intersection and RR the deduplicated round-robin sequence. Agreement-first emits all common IDs, followed by RR noncommon IDs, then truncates to three. Agreement-only emits I without filling unused slots. Disagreement-first promotes the RR noncommon IDs before common ones and is declared a negative control. Left-union and RR retain their previous definitions. Fixed-count rules emit min(3,|U|) IDs; agreement-only emits |I|, possibly zero. Disagreement here means nonoverlap of IDs, not contradiction between scientific claims.

Agreement-only has a simple containment limitation. Because each A contains at most three distinct IDs, left-union truncated at three still contains all of A, while I is a subset of A. Any rationale contained in I is therefore also contained in left-union. Agreement-only cannot improve sufficient containment over left-union under this contract. Removing extra IDs can nevertheless improve exact-reference matching, so an exact-score increase need not indicate newly recovered information. Empty intersection is retained as a zero-score output, not omitted from coverage.

We compute two exact uniform-subset controls on the same U: length min(3,|U|), and length |I| for that particular pair. The second isolates whether the intersection selects unusually useful IDs after matching its shortened output count. These probabilities enumerate all equally likely subsets; they are not random model trials. ID-count matching does not equate tokens, inference access, bytes or elapsed cost. The conditional correct-label and supplied-document assumptions remain unchanged.

sections.heading: Length-matched controls expose a reference-score tradeoff
paragraphs: The primary aggregate averages ordered pairs within each task, tasks within each recorded component, then the 204 components equally. Equal-task and pair-pooled alternatives remain separate. Of the 22,794 pairs, 5,407 contain a complete reference rationale in I, 15,132 contain one somewhere in U but not I, and 2,255 contain none in U. Agreement-only passes sufficient containment on exactly the first stratum. Its 13,855 sufficient losses versus left-union coexist with 2,328 exact gains and 22 exact losses. This is a measurement tradeoff on constructed responses, not a behavioral skill success/failure rate.

Agreement-only improves equal-component exact score from left-union 0.031228 to 0.150539 while reducing sufficient score from 0.789671 to 0.290889. It emits 20,604 IDs over all pairs, versus 58,284 for every fixed-count rule: pair-pooled average lengths 0.903922 and 2.556989 respectively. Against the pairwise length-matched uniform control, however, agreement-only is lower on both endpoints: sufficient 0.290889 versus 0.356638 and exact 0.150539 versus 0.221823. Thus its apparent exact gain against a longer rule cannot be credited to agreement information alone.

The bank includes 2,494 identical-input diagonal pairs and 20,300 distinct-input pairs; both sets still come from the same authored candidate lists. A distinct-input sensitivity keeps all 309 tasks and 204 components. Agreement-only remains below its matched-length random control: sufficient 0.240666 versus 0.311992 and exact 0.145307 versus 0.223723. Diagonal removal is a sensitivity, not a new independent cohort or a replacement primary denominator.

Agreement-first has 1,113 sufficient gains and 71 losses against left-union, but that bundled comparison also changes the noncommon ordering from left priority to RR. We inspected its first saved loss before writing a mechanistic claim and found that the common ID was already at the front. That example cannot identify the separate effect of promoting agreement. We therefore preserve the original primary run and add a separately planned, explicitly post-primary priority audit with a common RR baseline.

sections.heading: A controlled agreement-priority counterexample
paragraphs: The auxiliary priority plan was written after the primary result and witness inspection. It reuses the same frozen pair records without changing the primary plan or candidate class. Against RR, agreement-first changes only the priority of common versus noncommon IDs: all common IDs fit within three, and the relative noncommon order stays fixed. This controlled finite intervention produces zero sufficient gains, two sufficient losses and 22,792 ties, with equal-component difference -1/13,056. Exact scores are tied on all 22,794 pairs. These observations are descriptive, not proof that agreement promotion must always lose.

The saved task scifact_v4_382 provides the actual counterexample. A=(1,2,0) and B=(4,5,0) each contain a valid alternative, either (1,2) or (4,5). Their common ID is 0. RR emits (1,4,2) and passes by containing (1,2); agreement-first emits (0,1,4) and contains neither complete alternative. The same union, capacity and output count are preserved, and the loss comes from promoting the shared item at the expense of completing either alternative. The two counted losses are ordered-pair records, not two independent tasks or naturally observed skill collapses.

The same controlled audit finds 122 sufficient gains and five losses when disagreement-first is compared with RR; its exact scores also tie throughout. Thus the negative control is not universally safe either. We do not retrospectively admit it to the four-rule selector or claim a deployable winner. Its role is to expose how the chosen candidate class and the constructed reference distribution affect an apparent consensus result. These counts do not establish that overlapping sentences are semantically wrong or nonoverlapping ones correct.

sections.heading: Grouped rule selection does not repair the selection boundary
paragraphs: To keep a gold-aware chooser separate from a possible rule selector, the primary plan assigns each recorded component to fold int(component_SHA256[:16],16) mod 5. The five held-out component counts are 40, 38, 38, 42 and 46. For each fold, only the other components may choose among the four declared candidates: left-union, RR, agreement-first and agreement-only. Training criterion is the same equal-component mean, with fixed declaration-order ties. Sufficient and exact are separate objectives; no held-out component contributes to that fold's choice.

All five sufficient-objective folds choose RR; all five exact-objective folds choose agreement-only. Cross-fitted equal-component scores therefore equal those fixed rules: sufficient-objective score 0.835115 and exact-objective score 0.150539, with no added score from varying the selected rule. The cross-objective outcomes remain visible: the exact-selected rule has sufficient 0.290889, while the sufficient-selected rule has exact 0.029496. This stable-choice null result is retained rather than describing the fold procedure itself as an improvement.

The per-pair gold oracle over the same four candidates reaches 0.840200 sufficient and 0.153696 exact, exceeding the respective cross-fitted scores by 0.005085 and 0.003158. It uses the held-out reference to choose independently for each pair and endpoint, so it is a diagnostic class upper bound, not a deployable routing score. The predeclared disagreement-first negative control, excluded from this class, scores sufficient 0.842416 and can exceed that four-candidate oracle. There is no contradiction: a restricted-class maximum does not bound methods outside its class. Adding that method after seeing its result would be another selection step, not a validated improvement.

Component-disjoint folds prevent the same recorded component from appearing in both training and held-out roles for a particular decision. They do not erase the earlier exposure of all annotations and diagnostic designs. These are finite development reanalyses, not a secret final evaluation, independent model histories or a population estimate. We report exact fractions and paired changes without treating 22,794 constructed pairs or ten selection decisions as independent observations.

sections.heading: Agreement literature, fair comparisons and the next admission gate
paragraphs: Self-consistency [20] samples multiple reasoning paths and aggregates their final answers. Our intersection signal concerns sentence IDs in two fixed constructed evidence lists; no reasoning-path sampling, majority answer vote or native self-consistency benchmark is implemented. The agreement question is relevant, but importing that method's published accuracy or treating sentence overlap as its mechanism would conflate different information contracts.

Cawley and Talbot [21] discuss overfitting a finite-data selection criterion and resulting evaluation bias. We reviewed the official abstract rather than transferring a theorem. The component-held-out rule chooser makes local selection rights explicit but cannot retrospectively make an exposed diagnostic bank independent. Prior SciFact, ERASER and SkillsBench distinctions remain: supplied-reference agreement is not model faithfulness, correct-label component scoring is not native end-to-end verification, and an unrun native skill benchmark is not qualified A/B composition evidence.

Both the primary audit and post-primary priority audit freeze plans, code, alternative verifiers and input bytes before their own output generation. Separate author checks reconstruct all 113,970 deterministic outputs, 25,119 uniform probability cells, 48 aggregate rows and ten fold choices; the auxiliary verifier reaggregates four controlled contrasts from 22,794 saved pairs. These are alternate implementations by the same author, not external peer review. Actual independent A/B authoring histories and qualified pairs remain zero; the target behavioral composition effect remains null.

The next study must freeze the candidate class, exact output/label contract and actual token/call costs before collecting independently authored, Q-qualified A/B responses on a reserved S cohort. It should test simple RR, agreement promotion, intersection and predeclared negative controls with all failures and empty eligibility retained. A successful correction on this exposed construction cannot substitute for that evidence. The immediate recommendation is a stronger comparison contract, not deployment of the highest post-hoc score.

sections.heading: Capacity windows separate order effects from scorer truncation
paragraphs: A new predeclared finite audit keeps the round-robin relative order within common and noncommon IDs and only promotes the common class. For a nested output prefix L, the first sufficient capacity is the minimum, over complete reference alternatives, of the largest reference-ID rank. Two operators therefore differ in sufficiency on at most one contiguous capacity interval for a fixed pair. This is an annotation-containment identity, not a semantic claim about agreeing natural skills.

We evaluated 22,794 existing ordered pairs at capacities0..6, retaining309 tasks and204 components. Full-output sufficient gain/loss counts are565/2700 atcap1,95/25 atcap2,0/2 atcap3 and0/0 atcap4..6. The first-three endpoint still has0/2 atcap4..6: a larger generated output does not remove a grader's first-three restriction. Capacities count output IDs; token and invocation costs remain unmeasured.

In the declared <=3-ID input class, if both inputs are individually annotation-sufficient, stable common promotion cannot lose full-output sufficiency at capacity>=4. An empty intersection leaves the baseline unchanged; it does not imply that both outputs succeed. Exhaustive authored certificates cover3,046 input pairs and122,571 one/two-alternative reference families. They verify the stated finite boundary and include overlapping alternatives, rather than adding new independent observations.

sections.heading: Discussion and Limitations
paragraphs: The strongest warranted conclusion is a prerequisite decision: admit the measurement contract before interpreting a qualified-composition contrast. The audit demonstrates particular failure modes in an incomplete grader and particular order sensitivity in a ranked endpoint. It does not demonstrate that combining real skill files generally lowers completion.

sections.heading: A behavioral study that could falsify the hypothesis
paragraphs: A next study must justify new source/history separation and access controls rather than rename the exposed tasks. Freeze the ancestor, resource graph, author contexts, proposal cap, Q gain rule, final endpoint, and AB order before S. Retain failed proposals and nonqualifiers. Use Q only for qualification, not retrospective repair based on S. If no pair qualifies, report yield zero and effect null; weakening the gate after seeing joint failure would redefine the target.

For eligible pairs, allocate fresh matched S0/A/B/AB resets. Keep all assigned availability cells, including nonactivation, invalid output, agent-caused timeout, and deliberate deferral. Unresolved external outages require a separate missingness ledger and bounded success summaries. Record installed, routed, read, and assembled hashes. Diagnostics should include BA order, tokenizer-matched irrelevant context, structured padding, unchanged-resource controls, and sham repair. A negative required-ranking score remains operational loss even if semantic-loss attribution is falsified.

Repeated trials share histories and source families. An inferential plan must say whether histories and families are fixed or sampled, and model both dependencies for claims about both populations. Qualification yield and paired variability from an independent feasibility pilot should inform later precision requirements; zero current histories cannot support a power claim. The semantic-interference explanation is weakened if the negative contrast vanishes when full evidence, ordering, tokenizer length, rights, and the declared grader are controlled.

sections.heading: Strong comparisons and accounting
paragraphs: A fixed-pool adapter comparison would give every policy identical candidate bytes, development feedback, tool rights, and total budget. Conservative replay must be allowed to narrow, reject, or fall back; an always-merge straw controller is insufficient. Typed migration must preserve the task contract and pass behavior checks, not receive credit for schema legality alone. Assessment-based assembly must retain router/assembler costs and information access. Naive concatenation is a separate control, not native SkillCAT v2 [16].

A native-system comparison is a different experiment: generation procedures, teacher/reference access, training objectives, routing, and assembly all matter. We have executed neither that experiment nor the fixed-pool adapters. Candidate-conditioned stress sets [17] can diagnose a policy but cannot estimate unselected prevalence. Instruction/content/resource controls [18] and versioned workflow packages [19] are useful extensions only after their own rights, environments, and contracts are frozen.

Charge candidate creation, rejected proposals and repairs, replay, routing, assembly, loading/cache, retries, and final execution. Q/S research overhead can be reported separately but remains part of total resource use. Compare completion alongside deferral, conditional deployment coverage, and cost; a policy that avoids every hard deployment must not appear unconditionally superior. No native-paper score is placed beside the local diagnostic counts as if measured on one benchmark.

sections.heading: Threats to interpretation
paragraphs: Gold labels and rationale sets are privileged inputs. Their semantic correctness and completeness were not independently adjudicated. A sentence outside the annotation union is unannotated by construction; calling it irrelevant is operational shorthand, not a domain-expert judgment. Exact-annotated can reject valid unlisted evidence, and sufficient containment tolerates unhelpful extras. Our conclusions concern the specified annotation contract.

The study uses one exposed scientific-verification adaptation. Structural disjointness does not establish semantic independence or absence of model pretraining exposure. Four paired flips and one unreachable case are finite findings worth preserving, not a population prevalence claim. The related-work inspection is bounded to recorded primary passages; several references are preprints, one uses an abstract-only scope, and none supplies a reproduced external result. No external professor or independent scientific reviewer endorsed the results.

The elementary reachability proof and counterexample do not certify methodological novelty. We do not show a new integration controller, general harm from skills, or superiority over the cited systems. The falsifiable contribution is narrower: concrete admissibility checks and controls prevent unsupported inferences in the planned qualified-composition experiment. Full reference scopes, local provenance, and reproducibility limits are preserved in the appendices and companion records.

The new support certificate is complete only under the declared ordered-ID response contract and its checked outside-union condition. It does not adjudicate unannotated valid rationales or model-generated labels. Its sharpness permits arm/task-specific response choices, without common-program, routing, qualification or learning constraints. These deliberately weak behavioral restrictions make the envelope conservative for actual skills and unsuitable as an empirical rate. Changing benchmark annotations, response validity, weighting or Q selection requires a new certificate or transport analysis. The total-variation bound additionally requires common preselection weights and fixed candidates; it does not absorb authoring changes or final-data feedback.

sections.heading: Conclusion
paragraphs: Before asking whether useful skills fail together, specify which outcomes would count and whether valid answers can be expressed. On the preserved SciFact adaptation, original alternatives, a three-ID cap, and evidence ordering change diagnostic acceptance in quantitatively different ways. These results support grader-admission decisions and narrower mechanism claims. Qualified composition remains a separate empirical question: with zero actual histories, its effect is null. The next defensible advance is an independently qualified, freshly evaluated behavioral study with strong conservative comparisons and complete accounting.

The new v14 analysis closes a narrower gap: it computes exact response-support envelopes and distinguishes their fixed-cohort meaning from qualification-cohort transport. The observed zero envelope at budgets at most three and the large budget-four worst case change how a future score sign should be audited. They do not supply missing qualified histories. The next decisive evidence remains an independently authored, fully charged A/B-to-S experiment with an unchanged declared task contract.

The constrained v15 replay adds a concrete falsification control: a sufficient-score gain and an exact-score loss coexist under a sentence-preserving union, while a three-ID cap introduces real omission. This is a measurement-and-operator result. It narrows what a future negative behavioral score would mean without supplying the still absent qualified histories.

The v16 orbit benchmark makes one repair claim precise: reversing priority fixes all selected cap-three losses but cannot improve a reversal-symmetric cohort. Matched simple controls and an exhaustive reference-conditional failure partition locate a future intervention's burden of proof. Round-robin containment gains with exact-match losses remain finite development evidence; qualified behavioral effects still await independent histories.

V17 shows that common-ID agreement, shortening and model selection require separate controls. A same-RR priority intervention has two actual sufficient failures; intersection-only trades coverage for exact agreement and still trails a length-matched random subset. Component cross-fitting adds no score over its stable fixed choices. The oracle is restricted to four predeclared rules, while excluded negative-control results remain diagnostic. None of these finite findings identifies a qualified behavioral skill-composition effect.

V19 identifies the capacity mechanism more precisely. Completing an alternative reference set is controlled by its maximum output rank; a stable common-item promotion creates at most one contiguous gain or loss window. For two individually annotation-sufficient inputs of length at most three, full-sufficiency loss is impossible at cap four or above. First-three scoring can nevertheless retain the earlier losses, and cap-one pooled and equal-component contrasts have opposite signs. These exact conditional statements refine the finite mechanism claim; they do not establish a behavioral effect of independently authored executable skills.

appendices.heading: Completeness and sharpness of the new response-support certificate
paragraphs: Let the annotation family be nonempty and contain no empty set; let d be an ID outside its union. For any response L, T(L) and E(L) imply U(L). The empty response witnesses (0,0,0) at cost zero. If E(L)=1, its full set equals an annotation R. Enumerating each min(3,|R|)-ID prefix subset of R enumerates every possible T score for that exact set, so the recorded minimum length is complete for (1,0,1) and (1,1,1).

If U=T=1 and E=0, the scored prefix contains an annotation R of size at most three. Any such nonexact response has length at least |R|+1. The response R followed by d has exactly that length, keeps U=T=1, and cannot equal any original annotation because d occurs in none. This proves both attainability and minimum length for (1,1,0).

If U=1,T=0,E=0, L has at least four IDs. Its three-ID prefix P contains no annotation, and some annotation R lies in L. Let W=P union R. If W is not an annotation, P followed by R minus P is a witness no longer than L. If W is an annotation, L must have at least one further ID because L is not exact. Appending d to the reduced witness therefore still fits within |L|. The prefix remains unsuccessful and the outside ID guarantees nonexactness. Exhausting P and R is consequently complete and retains a minimum-length (1,0,0) witness. These five cases exhaust all possible patterns. The outside-union assumption is necessary for this particular reduction argument; its failure must be detected rather than hidden.

For discrepancy e_t(L)=g(L)-h(L), the change in a three-arm mean-isolated contrast is e_t(L_AB) minus half the sum of e_t(L_A) and e_t(L_B). This lies in the interval from m_t-M_t to M_t-m_t. Finite support attains both endpoints by choosing minimizing/maximizing witnesses. Because no cross-task or cross-arm realizability restriction is imposed, nonnegative fixed weights preserve sharpness after summation. Imposing a shared learned program or information constraints can shrink the attainable set, so the certificate remains an outer bound rather than a claim that qualified agents attain it.

For two selected distributions derived from the same original weights, their common probability mass after normalization is r/max(q_g,q_h). Total variation equals one minus that overlap. A bounded function in [-1,1] has expectation difference at most twice total variation, attained by assigning +1 and -1 according to the sign of the distribution difference. An authored three-history example checks equality. If an admission mass is zero, normalization is undefined and no point effect or overlap correction is supplied.

A proposed next feasibility pilot uses three independently sourced task families and four independent authoring attempts per family: twelve attempted A/B histories, not a power-calculated confirmatory sample. The two authors receive the common ancestor, public D information and identical tool rights, but not each other's patch or auditor-only Q/S labels. Cap each branch at two proposals and preserve every rejection, invalid proposal and failed call. Before authoring, freeze the actual model identity, request/token/cost limits, rationale contract and tokenizer-aware budget. Use twenty source-disjoint Q tasks per family and one predeclared seed; require each isolated branch to exceed the same ancestor by at least two successful tasks out of twenty. Freeze all capped proposals before Q and return no Q feedback to their authors. An auditor chooses the first passing proposal in the predeclared proposal order for each branch, not the best final-S result. With one ancestor and at most four branch proposals, qualification costs at most one hundred task-arm executions per history, before charged generation and tool work. This is a fixed feasibility rule, not a powered significance test, and permits no final-S repair. The number of eligible pairs is an outcome: do not relax the gate if it is zero.

For each eligible pair, a bounded first S phase would assign four fresh reset arms on twenty unexposed tasks per family with two predeclared seeds per arm, up to 160 final task-arm-seed executions per pair. Twenty tasks and two seeds are feasibility caps, not an asserted precision or independence guarantee. A third party or user must provide genuinely unexposed source histories/tasks, and the evaluation package must preserve their access log. Record all four frozen outputs before endpoint rescoring, a union-of-Q-gates cohort ledger if testing qualification changes, complete availability/routing/read/assembly traces, rejected proposals and total resource use.
